  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and dwesley@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to
the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:0
a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and prio
to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Of
of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and prio
to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Of
of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and dwesley@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the
scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  January 14, 2025

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 14, 2025, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Angela Allen  City Treasurer
  Louis A. Atwell  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Jose Cortes  Assistant City Manager
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Destinee Wesley  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS. Mayor Butts addressed the devastating wildfires that
  took place in the Los Angeles, Eaton, and Altadena areas. He reported that the fires have
  tragically resulted in 24 deaths, with 40,558 acres being destroyed, including 12,000 homes
  and businesses.

  The Mayor acknowledged the efforts of Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, Los Angeles
  County Fire Chief Anthony Maronne, Los Angeles Police Chief Jim McDonnell, and the
  dedicated 47,000 firefighters and law enforcement officers who are actively working to
  combat the fires. He also expressed gratitude to the Inglewood Police Department for their
  support in these efforts.

  Mayor Butts Commented that Agenda Item No. DR-1 was pulled from the Agenda.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if
  there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agenda, other the
  public hearings.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning Agenda item DR-1, however this item was
  pulled from the Agenda.

142.9  PAYMENT WARRANTS AND BILLS – RECEIVED AND FILED. The demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated January 10, 2025,
  in the amount of $6,849,942.69 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said register that
  said demand is received and filed.

  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts ordered the
  Warrants and Bills received and filed.
 January 14, 2025

125  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 25-01 ADOPTED- AMENDING
  CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 5 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE. The City
  Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider adoption of
  Ordinance No. 25-01, amending Chapter 2 (Administration), Article 5 (Purchasing) of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code, that notice has been given in the time, form, and manner as
  required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communication were received.

  Louis Atwell, City Manager presented the Staff Report dated January, 14, 2025

  Sharon Kioke, Finance Director, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:10 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that Ordinance No. 25-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 5 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO UPDATE THE PURCHASING ORDINANCE

  which was introduced at the meeting held on November 19, 2024, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION (EA-CE-2024-114)
  AFFIRMED; ORDINANCE NO. 25-04 INTRODUCED – ESTABLISHING
  OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS IN CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public
  hearing to consider introduction of an Ordinance approving Zoning Code Amendment No.
  24-00001 (ZCA24-00001) to establish objective design standards in Chapter 12 of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code, Citywide, that notice has been given in the time, form, and
  manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communication were received.

  Louis Atwell City Manager presented the Staff Report dated January 14, 2025.

  Bernard McCrumby, Developmental Services Planner Manger department presented an oral
  report regarding Zoning Code Amendment No 24-00001.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.
